deviceResetHints.t5ai: DTR/RTS download-mode pulse (longer hold)—same timing as the link handshake when connecting. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.t1: Same as T5AI: DTR/RTS download-mode pulse (longer hold)—same timing as the link handshake when connecting. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.t3: DTR/RTS pulse with longer hold—same handshake family when connecting. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.t2: DTR/RTS shorter pulse—same as the handshake when connecting. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.bk7231n: DTR/RTS shorter pulse matching the connect handshake. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.esp32: USB–UART hard-reset sequence (same as after a flash completes; line mapping depends on the board). Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.esp32c3: Reset follows the detected USB serial/JTAG path—same as post-flash reset. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.esp32c6: Hard reset matches post-flash reset; interface type is auto-detected. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.esp32p4: Hard reset matches post-flash reset; interface type is auto-detected. Free the serial port first.
deviceResetHints.esp32s3: Some boards use a USB-JTAG/serial bridge; reset timing matches post-flash reset. Free the serial port first.

disclaimer.title: ⚠️ Important Notice Before Use

item1.title: Device MAC Address Uniqueness
item1.body: Every authorized device must have a globally unique MAC address. This tool does not validate MAC conflicts across devices. The operator is solely responsible for ensuring each device's MAC is unique. Authorization credentials are bound to the MAC address. Duplicate MACs cause different devices to share the same authorization code, undermining credential uniqueness and leading to device identification failures on the Tuya platform.

item2.title: OTP Authorization Is Permanent and Irreversible
item2.body: When OTP storage mode is enabled with eFuse locking, authorization data is permanently burned into the chip and cannot be erased, modified, or revoked. Devices with a failed lock or interrupted write must be physically isolated from the production line for manual verification before any further use or shipment.

item3.title: Keep the Authorization Excel File Secure
item3.body: The Excel file contains sensitive device credentials (UUID / Key). Keep it secure, prevent unauthorized access, and back it up after operations.

item4.title: Devices with Default MAC Cannot Be Authorized
item4.body: T5AI chips without firmware return a default MAC address. This tool automatically rejects authorization for such devices. Ensure firmware is correctly flashed before running authorization.

item5.title: Operator Responsibility
item5.body: This tool assists batch operations. The operator and production line supervisor are solely responsible for MAC uniqueness, authorization integrity, and product compliance.
